claims.statement: Carcamán also means a big, heavy boat and, by extension, a lazy man or a frail old man.
claims.statement_id: Kata carcamán juga berarti kapal besar yang berat, dan secara kiasan lelaki malas atau lelaki tua yang sakit-sakitan.
claims.quote: Baixo o termo de carcamán tamén se designa un barco grande e pesado e, por extensión, un home lacazán que non quere facer esforzos ou ben un home vello e achacoso.

claims.statement: Some historians believe the term originally meant Italian merchants sailing from Italy to Flanders and stopping in Galicia in the 17th and 18th centuries.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sejarawan percaya istilah ini awalnya merujuk pedagang Italia yang berlayar dari Italia ke Flandria dan singgah di Galisia pada abad ke-17 dan ke-18.
claims.quote: Alguns historiadores acreditam que o termo se referia originalmente aos comerciantes italianos que navegavam da Península Itálica até à Flandres, parando na Galiza durante os séculos XVII e XVIII.

claims.statement: Another hypothesis holds the term described the smugglers of Arousa, especially in wartime and after.
claims.statement_id: Hipotesis lain menyebut istilah ini dipakai untuk penyelundup Arousa, terutama pada masa perang dan sesudahnya.
claims.quote: Outra hipótese sugere que o termo foi usado para descrever os contrabandistas da Arousa, especialmente durante os períodos de guerra e pós-guerra

claims.statement: The Real Academia Galega dictionary (1913-1928) records that sailors in Galicia call smugglers carcamáns.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Real Academia Galega (1913-1928) mencatat bahwa para pelaut di Galisia menyebut penyelundup dengan nama carcamán.
claims.quote: Los marineros, en Galicia , llaman así a los contrabandistas.

claims.statement: The same dictionary, quoting Murguía, says the name is used in the Rías Bajas for those of the island of Arosa, because in 1826 Italian smugglers were masters of the place.
claims.statement_id: Kamus yang sama, mengutip Murguía, mengatakan bahwa di Rías Baixas nama itu dipakai untuk penduduk pulau Arosa, karena pada tahun 1826 penyelundup Italia menguasai pulau itu.
claims.quote: Llaman así en las Rías Bajas a los de la isla de Arosa . Viene esto de que el año 1826 estuvieron los contrabandistas italianos siendo dueños de aquello.

claims.statement: According to the Portuguese article, Alfredo García Alén's catalogue records at the Museu de Pontevedra on the Arousa archaeological digs mention the Carcamáns as a race of giants usually linked in Galician mythology to the castro culture.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel berbahasa Portugis, dalam catatan katalog Alfredo García Alén dari Museu de Pontevedra tentang penggalian arkeologi Arousa, para Carcamáns disebut ras raksasa yang dalam mitologi Galisia biasanya dikaitkan dengan budaya castro.
claims.quote: menciona que os Carcamáns são uma raça de gigantes, geralmente ligados na mitologia galega à cultura castreja.

claims.statement: The Dicionário de seres míticos galegos (Cuba, Reigosa, Miranda) says only that they are a 'race of mythical pirates of the island of Arousa'.
claims.statement_id: Dicionário dos seres míticos galegos (Cuba, Reigosa, Miranda) hanya menyebut mereka "ras bajak laut mitis dari pulau Arousa".
claims.quote: O Dicionário dos seres míticos galegos de Cuba, Reigosa e Miranda apenas diz que são uma “raça de piratas míticos da ilha de Arousa”.

claims.statement: In Castelao's short piece, a woman under an enchantment is said to live in the 'cova dos carcamáns' (cave of the carcamáns) and to come and comb her hair early in the morning on the rocks by the shore.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah pendek Castelao, di "cova dos carcamáns" (gua para carcamán) konon tinggal seorang perempuan terpesona yang datang menyisir rambut pagi-pagi di batu-batu tepi laut.
claims.quote: vive —según contan— unha dona encantada que vén a peitearse de mañán cedo nas pedras da beiramar

claims.statement: The carmençó is a spirit (geni) of Catalan mythology that roams mountain meadows, black as soot and woolly from head to toe.
claims.statement_id: Carmençó adalah roh (geni) mitologi Katalan yang berkeliaran di padang rumput gunung, hitam seperti jelaga dan berbulu wol dari kepala sampai kaki.
claims.quote: El carmençó és un geni de la mitologia catalana, que ronda pels prats de muntanya, negre com el sutge i llanut de cap a peus.

claims.statement: It is both feared and respected by the old shepherds of the Empordà, since seeing it brings many years of misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Ia ditakuti sekaligus dihormati para gembala tua Empordà, karena melihatnya membawa bertahun-tahun kemalangan.
claims.quote: És un ésser temut i respectat alhora pels vells pastors empordanesos, perquè veure'l comporta molts anys de desgràcia.

claims.statement: The Basque article also notes it is feared and respected by the old shepherds of the Empordà because it brings years of misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Basque juga mencatat bahwa ia ditakuti dan dihormati para gembala tua Empordà karena membawa bertahun-tahun kemalangan.
claims.quote: Empordàko artzain zaharrek aldi berean beldurtzen eta errespetatzen duten izaki bat da, urte askotako zorigaitza baitakar.

claims.statement: It settles in the shepherds' huts when they are not in use, mainly in winter, keeping them from collapsing.
claims.statement_id: Ia menempati pondok-pondok gembala saat tidak dipakai, terutama di musim dingin, sehingga pondok itu tidak roboh.
claims.quote: S'instal·la a les cabanes dels pastors quan aquests no les fan servir, principalment a l'hivern, evitant que s'esfondrin.

claims.statement: For this reason, when they come up from the lowlands, the shepherds sling seven stones to drive it out of the hut.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu, ketika naik dari dataran rendah, para gembala melemparkan tujuh batu dengan ketapel untuk mengusirnya dari pondok.
claims.quote: És per aquest motiu que, quan pugen de terra baixa, llencen set pedrades amb la fona per foragitar-lo de la cabana.

claims.statement: According to the Basque article, Carmenço is a genius of Catalan mythology that roams mountain meadows, black as soot and hairy from foot to head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel berbahasa Basque, Carmenço adalah genius mitologi Katalan yang berkeliaran di padang rumput gunung, hitam seperti jelaga dan berbulu dari kaki sampai kepala.
claims.quote: Carmenço mitologia katalaneko jenio bat da, mendiko belardietan ibiltzen dena, kedarra bezain beltza eta iletsua, oinetik burura.

claims.statement: The Cegua (from Nahuatl cihuatl, 'woman'), also known as Ceguanaba, Segua or Tzegua, is a figure of Mexican and Central American legend.
claims.statement_id: Cegua (dari bahasa Nahuatl cihuatl, "perempuan"), dikenal juga sebagai Ceguanaba, Segua, atau Tzegua, adalah tokoh legenda Meksiko dan Amerika Tengah.
claims.quote: La Cegua (del náhuatl, cihuatl, mujer),​​ también conocida como Ceguanaba,​ Segua o Tzegua, es un personaje de las leyendas mexicanas y centroamericanas.

claims.statement: It is a spectral being that appears at night on lonely roads asking to be taken to a nearby village; it usually appears to womanisers as a very beautiful woman who then turns into a monster with a horse's head.
claims.statement_id: Ia makhluk hantu yang muncul malam hari di jalan sepi, meminta diantar ke desa terdekat; biasanya ia menampakkan diri kepada lelaki hidung belang sebagai perempuan sangat cantik yang lalu berubah menjadi monster berkepala kuda.
claims.quote: Es un ser espectral que se materializa por las noches en caminos solitarios, solicitando ayuda para que la lleven a algún poblado cercano. El espanto generalmente se aparece a los hombres mujeriegos en la forma de una mujer muy hermosa, la cual luego se transforma en un monstruo con la cabeza de un caballo.

claims.statement: The Cegua myth is Mesoamerican in origin and related to the Siguanaba myth and partly to La Llorona.
claims.statement_id: Mitos Cegua berasal dari Mesoamerika dan berkaitan dengan mitos Siguanaba serta sebagian dengan La Llorona.
claims.quote: El mito de la Cegua es de origen mesoamericano y está relacionado con el mito de la Siguanaba, con algunas variantes, y en parte, con el de la Llorona.

claims.statement: Like the Cadejo legend, the Cegua arose from cultural syncretism after the Spaniards arrived, since the horse face did not exist in pre-Hispanic times.
claims.statement_id: Seperti legenda Cadejo, Cegua lahir dari sinkretisme budaya setelah kedatangan orang Spanyol, karena wajah kuda belum dikenal pada masa pra-Hispanik.
claims.quote: Al igual que con la leyenda del Cadejo, entonces, la Cegua proviene del sincretismo cultural que se insertó con la llegada de los españoles a América, ya que el concepto del rostro de caballo aún no existía en los tiempos prehispánicos

claims.statement: The term cegua is used mainly in Nicaragua and Costa Rica.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan cegua terutama dipakai di Nikaragua dan Kosta Rika.
claims.quote: El término cegua para designar a este ser espectral es de uso predominante en Nicaragua y Costa Rica

claims.statement: According to the Norwegian article, once she is up on the horse, or vehicle in modern versions, she turns into a dreadful creature with a rotting horse skull for a head.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Norwegia, setelah naik ke kuda, atau kendaraan dalam versi modern, ia berubah menjadi makhluk mengerikan berkepala tengkorak kuda yang membusuk.
claims.quote: Når hun har satt seg opp på hesten, eller kjøretøyet i moderne versjoner av legenden, forvandler hun seg til en fryktelig skapning med en råtnende hestehodeskalle som hode.

claims.statement: The Coulobre is a fantastic creature, a kind of drac or dragon, that haunted the spring of Fontaine-de-Vaucluse.
claims.statement_id: Coulobre adalah makhluk khayalan, semacam drac atau naga, yang menghantui mata air Fontaine-de-Vaucluse.
claims.quote: Le Coulobre est une créature fantastique, sorte de drac ou dragon, qui hantait la fontaine de Vaucluse.

claims.statement: According to legend, Saint Véran, bishop of Cavaillon, miraculously rid the river Sorgue of it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Santo Véran, uskup Cavaillon, secara ajaib membebaskan sungai Sorgue darinya.
claims.quote: Selon la légende, saint Véran, évêque de Cavaillon, en aurait miraculeusement débarrassé la rivière Sorgue.

claims.statement: It was a winged creature living in the spring of the Sorgue; it supposedly mated with dragons who then abandoned it, leaving it to raise alone the little black, gold-spotted salamanders it bore.
claims.statement_id: Ia makhluk bersayap yang hidup di mata air Sorgue; konon ia kawin dengan naga-naga yang lalu meninggalkannya, sehingga ia harus membesarkan sendiri anak-anaknya, salamander hitam berbintik emas.
claims.quote: était une créature ailée qui vivait dans l'exsurgence de la Sorgue. Elle passait pour s'unir avec des dragons qui l'abandonnaient ensuite, le forçant à élever seul les petites salamandres noires tachetées d'or dont elle accouchait.

claims.statement: Véran drove off 'this foul beast', which flew to the Alps to die, supposedly at the village of Saint-Véran, where it is carved under the church porch.
claims.statement_id: Véran mengusir "binatang najis" itu, yang terbang ke Pegunungan Alpen dan mati di sana, konon di desa Saint-Véran, tempat patungnya ada di bawah serambi gereja.
claims.quote: Selon la légende, Véran chassa « cette bête immonde » qui s'envola vers les Alpes où elle s'en fut mourir. Le village de Saint-Véran aurait été son lieu de chute. Le monstre se trouve d'ailleurs statufié sous le porche de l'église.

claims.statement: In the 15th-century revival of the myth, Petrarch was supposedly attacked by the creature by the water with his beloved and killed it with his sword, but Laura later died of the plague.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebangkitan mitos abad ke-15, Petrarca konon diserang makhluk ini di tepi air bersama kekasihnya dan membunuhnya dengan pedang, tetapi Laura kemudian mati karena wabah.
claims.quote: Pétrarque aurait été attaqué par cette créature alors qu'il se trouvait au bord de l'eau avec sa bien-aimée : il tua le monstre d'un coup d'épée mais Laure mourut ensuite de la peste.

claims.statement: The Coulobre is mentioned in the video game Dordogne, released in 2023.
claims.statement_id: Coulobre disebut dalam permainan video Dordogne yang dirilis pada 2023.
claims.quote: Le Coulobre est évoqué dans le jeu vidéo Dordogne, sorti en 2023.

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, the Coulobre is female, living alone and seeking a mate.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, Coulobre adalah makhluk betina yang hidup sendirian dan mencari pasangan.
claims.quote: По легенде Кулобр — существо женского рода. Она живёт в одиночестве и пытается найти себе пару.

claims.statement: The dipsa is a tiny, mucus-like, extremely venomous snake of medieval bestiaries, so venomous that its victim died before realising he had been bitten.
claims.statement_id: Dipsa adalah ular mungil mirip lendir yang sangat berbisa dalam bestiari abad pertengahan; bisanya begitu kuat sehingga korbannya mati sebelum sadar telah digigit.
claims.quote: Dipsa is a tiny, mucus-like, extremely venomous snake from Medieval bestiaries. They were so venomous that their victim would die before becoming aware he had been bitten.

claims.statement: The Italian article likewise calls the dipsa a tiny, extremely venomous snake of medieval bestiaries.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Italia juga menyebut dipsa ular mungil yang sangat berbisa dalam bestiari abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: La dipsa è un minuscolo serpente estremamente velenoso diffuso nei bestiari medievali.

claims.statement: Isidore of Seville (Etymologies 12.4.13) calls the dipsas a kind of asp, called situla in Latin because anyone bitten by it dies of thirst.
claims.statement_id: Isidorus dari Sevilla (Etymologies 12.4.13) menyebut dipsas sebagai sejenis ular asp yang dalam bahasa Latin disebut situla karena siapa pun yang digigitnya mati kehausan.
claims.quote: Isidore of Seville [7th century CE] (Etymologies, Book 12, 4.13; 12, 4.32): [Book 12, 4.13] The dipsas is a kind of asp, called situla in Latin because anyone bitten by it dies of thirst.

claims.statement: Isidore (Etymologies 12.4.32) writes that the dipsas is said to be a snake so tiny that it is not noticed when stepped on; its venom kills before it is felt, so the face of one about to die shows no horror of his impending death.
claims.statement_id: Isidorus (Etymologies 12.4.32) menulis bahwa dipsas konon ular yang begitu kecil sehingga tak terlihat saat terinjak; bisanya membunuh sebelum terasa, sehingga wajah orang yang akan mati tidak memperlihatkan kengerian akan kematiannya.
claims.quote: Isidore of Seville [7th century CE] ... [Book 12, 4:32] The dipsas is said to be a snake so tiny that when it is stepped on it is not observed. Its venom kills before it is felt, so that the face of one about to die displays no horror of his impending death.

claims.statement: Aelian (On the Characteristics of Animals 6.51) writes that the name Dipsas [thirst-provoker] declares what it does: it is smaller than the viper but kills more swiftly, for persons who chance to be bitten burn with thirst.
claims.statement_id: Aelianus (On the Characteristics of Animals 6.51) menulis bahwa nama Dipsas [pemicu rasa haus] menyatakan sifatnya: ia lebih kecil daripada ular beludak tetapi membunuh lebih cepat, karena orang yang kebetulan digigit terbakar oleh rasa haus.
claims.quote: Aelianus [170-230 CE] (On the Characteristics of Animals, Book 6, 51): The name of the Dipsas [thirst-provoker] declares to us what it does. It is smaller than the viper, but kills more swiftly, for persons who chance to be bitten burn with thirst

claims.statement: Gerald of Wales (Topographia Hibernica, distinction 1, chapter 26) mentions the dipsa as a small species of snake whose venom destroys life before it is perceived and is so powerful that its bite causes death before any pain is felt.
claims.statement_id: Gerald dari Wales (Topographia Hibernica, distinctio 1, bab 26) menyebut dipsa sebagai ular kecil yang bisanya menghancurkan nyawa sebelum disadari dan begitu kuat sehingga gigitannya menyebabkan kematian sebelum rasa sakit terasa.
claims.quote: Gerald of Wales [c. 1146 – c. 1223] (Topographia Hibernica, Distinction 1, chapter 26): There is also the dipsa, a small species of snake, whose venom destroys life before it is even perceived, and is so powerful that its bite occasions death before any pain is felt.

claims.statement: In Lucan's Pharsalia (book 9), Aulus of Tyrrhenia, a standard-bearer, trod on a dipsas; the serpent struck with its head reversed, and no pang betrayed the tooth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Pharsalia karya Lucan (buku 9), Aulus dari Tyrrhenia, pembawa panji, menginjak seekor dipsas; ular itu menyambar dengan kepala terbalik dan tak ada rasa sakit yang mengkhianati gigitan itu.
claims.quote: Lucan [1st century CE] (Pharsalia, book 9, verse 821-841): Tyrrhenian Aulus, bearer of a flag, / Trod on a dipsas ; quick with head reversed / The serpent struck ; no pang betrayed the tooth

claims.statement: In archaic Greek mythology Europa (Εὐρώπη) is an Oceanid and a Nephele (cloud nymph), daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, named by Hesiod in his list of Oceanids.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Yunani arkais, Europa (Εὐρώπη) adalah Okeanid sekaligus Nephele (nimfa awan), putri Okeanos dan Tethys yang disebut Hesiodos dalam daftar Okeanidnya.
claims.quote: Dans la mythologie grecque archaïque, Europe (en grec ancien Εὐρώπη / Eurôpê) est une Océanide et une Néphélée, fille d'Océan et de Téthys citée par Hésiode dans sa liste d'Océanides.

claims.statement: According to Hesiod's Theogony she brings rain to the European continent, whose name she may have inspired, though this is debated.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Theogonia karya Hesiodos ia membawa hujan ke benua Eropa, dan namanya mungkin menjadi asal nama benua itu, meski hal ini diperdebatkan.
claims.quote: Selon la Théogonie d'Hésiode, elle apporte la pluie sur le continent européen, dont elle pourrait être à l'origine du nom (ce point est débattu).

claims.statement: She is one of the many daughters of Oceanus and Tethys, usually three thousand, with three thousand brothers, the river gods.
claims.statement_id: Ia salah satu dari putri-putri Okeanos dan Tethys yang biasanya berjumlah tiga ribu, dengan tiga ribu saudara laki-laki para dewa sungai.
claims.quote: Elle est l'une de leur multiples filles, les Océanides, généralement au nombre de trois mille, et a pour frères les Dieux-fleuve, eux aussi au nombre de trois mille.

claims.statement: The Breton article likewise says that according to Hesiod's Theogony she brings rain to the continent of Europe.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Breton juga menyebut bahwa menurut Theogonia Hesiodos ia membawa hujan ke benua Eropa.
claims.quote: Hervez Theogonia Hesiodos eo ganti e vez degaset glav war zouar Europa, ar c'hevandir.

claims.statement: The Theoi Project describes Europe (Europa) as the Okeanis nymph of the continent of Europe, with a sister named Asia.
claims.statement_id: Theoi Project menyebut Europe (Europa) sebagai nimfa Okeanis dari benua Eropa, dengan saudarinya bernama Asia.
claims.quote: EUROPE (Europa) The Okeanis Nymphe of the continent of Europe. Her sister was Asia.

claims.statement: In Hesiod's Theogony (line 346 ff.), Europa is named in the list of the daughters of Tethys and Okeanos, among Menestho, Metis, Eurynome and Asia.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos (baris 346 dst.), Europa disebut dalam daftar putri Tethys dan Okeanos, di antara Menestho, Metis, Eurynome, dan Asia.
claims.quote: Perseis and Ianeira, Petraie the lovely, and Menestho, and Europa, Metis and Eurynome, Telesto robed in saffron, Khryseis, and Asia

claims.statement: Hesiod says there are three thousand light-stepping daughters of Okeanos scattered far and wide, bright children among the goddesses.
claims.statement_id: Hesiodos menyebut ada tiga ribu putri Okeanos yang melangkah ringan, tersebar luas, anak-anak cemerlang di antara para dewi.
claims.quote: there are three thousand light-stepping daughters of Okeanos scattered far and wide, bright children among the goddesses

claims.statement: The facanito is a child who masks as a careto and imitates the caretos in their revels, performing his own initiation rite and keeping the tradition alive.
claims.statement_id: Facanito adalah anak yang memakai topeng careto dan meniru para careto dalam pesta mereka, menjalankan ritual inisiasinya sendiri dan menjaga kelangsungan tradisi.
claims.quote: O facanito é uma criança que se mascara de “careto” e tenta imitar os caretos nas suas folias, cumprindo o seu próprio ritual de iniciação e garantindo a continuidade da tradição.

claims.statement: In the Middle Ages in Trás-os-Montes it was called 'a little devil that feeds on ground steel'; in Miranda do Douro the name is given to a small, provocative man, and also to a mythological being, very small and restless.
claims.statement_id: Pada Abad Pertengahan di Trás-os-Montes ia disebut "setan kecil yang makan baja tumbuk"; di Miranda do Douro namanya dipakai untuk lelaki bertubuh kecil yang suka memancing keributan, dan juga untuk makhluk mitologis yang sangat kecil dan gelisah.
claims.quote: Na Idade Média em Trás-os-Montes era referido como um "diabinho que se alimenta de aço moído". Em Miranda do Douro é o nome que se dá a um homem de pequena estatura com jeito de provocador e é também como se designa um ser mitológico, muito pequeno e irrequieto.

claims.statement: The careto is a masked figure of the carnival (Entrudo) of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro in Portugal.
claims.statement_id: Careto adalah tokoh bertopeng dalam karnaval (Entrudo) Trás-os-Montes dan Alto Douro di Portugal.
claims.quote: L careto ye ua figura maçcarada de l Antruido de  Trás ls Montes i Alto Douro, an Pertual.

claims.statement: The careto tradition is thought to have Celtic, pre-Roman roots.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi careto diduga berakar pada budaya Kelt pra-Romawi.
claims.quote: Pensa-se que la tradiçon de ls caretos tenga raízes célticas, de la era pré-romana.

claims.statement: According to the Mirandese article, the facanito or facanico is a child masked as a careto who tries to imitate the caretos at their festivals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel berbahasa Mirandés, facanito atau facanico adalah seorang anak yang mengenakan topeng careto dan berusaha meniru para careto dalam pesta mereka.
claims.quote: L facanito ó facanico ye un nino maçcarado de careto, que tenta eimitar ls caretos nas sues fiestas

claims.statement: According to the Lusa/RTP report, the procession is completed by the 'facanitos', the smallest children of the village, masked as mafarricos (little devils), accompanying the adults, performing their own initiation ritual and ensuring the continuity of the tradition.
claims.statement_id: Menurut laporan Lusa/RTP, arak-arakan dilengkapi "facanitos", yaitu anak-anak terkecil di desa yang bertopeng mafarrico (iblis kecil), menyertai orang dewasa, menjalani ritual inisiasi mereka sendiri dan menjamin kesinambungan tradisi.
claims.quote: O cortejo completa-se com os "facanitos", ou seja os mais pequenos da aldeia que, mascarados de mafarricos, acompanham os adultos, cumprindo o seu próprio ritual de iniciação e garantindo a continuidade da tradição.

claims.statement: According to oral-literature researcher Alexandre Parafita, speaking to Lusa, the 'diabolical' parades of caretos, matrafonas and facanitos are among the most genuine Entrudo (carnival) traditions in Trás-os-Montes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut peneliti sastra lisan Alexandre Parafita kepada Lusa, arak-arakan "diabolis" para caretos, matrafonas, dan facanitos termasuk tradisi Entrudo (karnaval) yang paling asli di Trás-os-Montes.
claims.quote: Os desfiles diabólicos de "caretos", "matrafonas" e "facanitos", as "pulhas casamenteiras" e as "leituras de testamentos" ou "papeladas", representam o mais genuíno das tradições do Entrudo em Trás-os-Montes, disse hoje à Lusa o investigador de literatura oral Alexandre Parafita.

claims.statement: Farfadets are creatures of French folklore; the word is rendered as sprite, imp, brownie or leprechaun, and they also resemble the pixies of Britain's West Country.
claims.statement_id: Farfadet adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Prancis; katanya dapat diterjemahkan sebagai sprite, imp, brownie, atau leprechaun, dan mereka juga mirip pixie dari West Country Britania.
claims.quote: Farfadets are creatures of French folklore. The word translates variously as "Sprite", "Imp",  "Brownie", or "Leprechaun", though they also resemble the Pixies of Britain's West Country.

claims.statement: The term is used throughout France, though the creature belongs especially to the Vendée and Poitou; farfadets also appear in Occitan mythology, especially in Provence, as fadets.
claims.statement_id: Istilah ini dipakai di seluruh Prancis, tetapi makhluknya khas Vendée dan Poitou; farfadet juga ada dalam mitologi Occitania, terutama di Provence, dengan nama fadet.
claims.quote: The term is in general use throughout France, though the creature is local particularly to the Vendée and Poitou regions. Farfadets also  feature in Occitan mythology, particularly in Provence, where they are known as fadets.

claims.statement: They are small (about half a metre tall), wrinkled and brown-skinned, usually in tattered brown clothes or naked.
claims.statement_id: Mereka kecil (sekitar setengah meter), keriput, dan berkulit cokelat, biasanya berpakaian cokelat compang-camping atau telanjang.
claims.quote: Farfadets are described as being small (some half-meter tall), wrinkled, and brown-skinned; they generally wear tattered brown clothing, or go naked.

claims.statement: They like to tend horses, grooming them or braiding their manes; they live in woods but also attach themselves to a nearby farm, doing odd jobs in the fields for a bowl of milk or cream left on the doorstep at night.
claims.statement_id: Mereka suka merawat kuda, menyisir atau mengepang surainya; mereka tinggal di hutan tetapi juga menempel pada pertanian terdekat dan mengerjakan tugas di ladang dengan imbalan semangkuk susu atau krim di depan pintu pada malam hari.
claims.quote: They like to tend horses, which they will groom, or weave ringlets into their manes. They live in woodland, but will also attach themselves to a neighbouring farm or homestead, and complete odd tasks in the fields, in return for a bowl of milk or cream left on the doorstep at night.

claims.statement: Yet too much kindness, such as leaving new clothes for them, can frighten them away.
claims.statement_id: Namun kebaikan yang berlebihan, seperti meninggalkan pakaian baru untuk mereka, dapat membuat mereka pergi.
claims.quote: However they can be frightened away by too much kindness, such as leaving new clothes out for them.

claims.statement: The French writer A. V. C. Berbiguier, who believed farfadets tormented him, published the autobiography Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde in 1821.
claims.statement_id: Penulis Prancis A. V. C. Berbiguier yang merasa disiksa farfadet menerbitkan otobiografi Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde pada 1821.
claims.quote: In 1821 he was constrained to publish an autobiography, Les Farfadets ou Tous les démons ne sont pas de l'autre monde

claims.statement: Farfadet is borrowed from 16th-century Provençal farfadet ('sprite'), probably an intensified form of fadet, itself from fada or fado, 'fairy'.
claims.statement_id: Kata farfadet dipinjam dari bahasa Provençal farfadet ("lutin") abad ke-16, mungkin bentuk penguat dari fadet, yang berasal dari fada atau fado, "peri".
claims.quote: Farfadet est un mot emprunté au provençal farfadet (« lutin ») du XVIe siècle, probablement forme renforcée de fadet, dérivé lui-même de fada, fado signifiant « fée ».

claims.statement: The Forest Bull is an animal of ancient and medieval bestiaries; according to Pliny the Elder they were fierce, tawny cattle of Ethiopia with mouths gaping to the ears and horns that, like a Yale's, could swivel any way.
claims.statement_id: Banteng Hutan adalah hewan bestiari kuno dan abad pertengahan; menurut Plinius Tua mereka sapi buas berwarna cokelat kekuningan di Etiopia dengan mulut menganga sampai telinga dan tanduk yang dapat berputar ke segala arah seperti tanduk Yale.
claims.quote: is an animal from ancient and medieval bestiaries. According to Pliny the Elder, they were a breed of ferocious, tawny cattle living in Ethiopia, with mouths gaping open to the ears. Their horns, like a Yale's, could swivel in any direction.

claims.statement: According to Aelian they were called 'flesh eaters', the fiercest of all animals, twice the size of ordinary bulls and very fast.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Aelianus mereka disebut "pemakan daging", hewan paling buas, dua kali lebih besar dari banteng biasa, dan sangat cepat berlari.
claims.quote: According to Aelian, they were called "flesh eaters" and were the most ferocious and savage of all animals. They were twice the size of regular bulls and could run at great speeds.

claims.statement: No weapon could hurt them, as spears, arrows and even iron glanced off their hide.
claims.statement_id: Tak ada senjata yang dapat melukai mereka, karena tombak, panah, bahkan besi memantul dari kulitnya.
claims.quote: No weapon could physically hurt the bulls, be it spears or arrows because even iron deflected from their skin.

claims.statement: To protect their flocks, local herdsmen dug deep ditches into which the bulls fell and choked on their own rage.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melindungi ternak, para gembala menggali parit dalam tempat banteng itu jatuh dan mati tercekik oleh amarahnya sendiri.
claims.quote: To protect their flocks, herdsmen who lived in the area dug deep ditches, in which the bulls would fall and consequently choke on their rage.

claims.statement: According to the Dutch article, the animal may be based on travellers' accounts of the African buffalo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Belanda, hewan ini mungkin berdasarkan catatan perjalanan tentang kerbau Afrika.
claims.quote: Mogelijk is dit dier gebaseerd op reisverslagen die de Afrikaanse buffel beschreven.

claims.statement: According to the Theoi Project, the Tauros Aithiopikos (Ethiopian Bull) was a ferocious breed of carnivorous bull native to Aithiopia (Ethiopia) in sub-Saharan Africa, with a thick red hide impervious to weapons.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Theoi Project, Tauros Aithiopikos (Banteng Etiopia) adalah jenis banteng buas pemakan daging asal Aithiopia (Etiopia) di Afrika sub-Sahara, dengan kulit merah tebal yang kebal senjata.
claims.quote: THE TAUROS AITHIOPIKOS (Ethiopian Bull) was a ferocious breed of carnivorous bull native to Aithiopia (Ethiopia) in sub-Saharan Africa. Its thick, red hide was impervious to weapons.

claims.statement: Pliny the Elder (Natural History 8.74) calls the Forest Bulls (Tauri Silvestres) the fiercest animals of Ethiopia: larger than field bulls, surpassing all in speed, tawny, blue-eyed, with backward-turned hair, mouth gaping to the ears and mobile horns, their hide as hard as flint and rejecting every wound.
claims.statement_id: Plinius Tua (Natural History 8.74) menyebut Banteng Hutan (Tauri Silvestres) sebagai hewan paling buas di Etiopia: lebih besar daripada banteng ladang, melampaui semua dalam kecepatan, berwarna cokelat kekuningan, bermata biru, berbulu mengarah ke belakang, bermulut menganga sampai telinga dan bertanduk yang dapat digerakkan; kulitnya sekeras batu api dan menolak setiap luka.
claims.quote: But its fiercest animals are the Forest Bulls (Tauri Silvestres), larger than the bulls of the field, surpassing all in speed, of a tawny colour, with blue eyes, hair turned backward, mouth gaping open to the ears, along with mobile horns; the hide has the hardness of flint, rejecting every wound.

claims.statement: According to Pliny the Elder, they hunt all wild animals but can themselves only be caught in pits, and when caught always die game.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Plinius Tua, banteng-banteng itu memburu semua hewan liar, tetapi sendiri hanya dapat ditangkap dalam lubang jebakan, dan bila tertangkap selalu mati dengan gagah.
claims.quote: They hunt all wild animals, but themselves can only be caught in pits, and when caught always die game.

claims.statement: According to Aelian (On Animals 17.45), their hair is red and their eyes blue-grey, more so than the eyes of lions.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Aelianus (On Animals 17.45), bulu mereka merah dan mata mereka abu-abu kebiruan, lebih daripada mata singa.
claims.quote: Their hair is red, their eyes blue-grey, more so than the eyes of lions.

claims.statement: According to Aelian, among the Troglodytoi (cave-dwellers) this animal is judged the king of beasts, for it has the courage of a lion, the speed of a horse, the strength of a bull and is stronger than iron.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Aelianus, di kalangan Troglodytoi (penghuni gua) hewan ini dianggap raja binatang, karena memiliki keberanian singa, kecepatan kuda, kekuatan banteng, dan lebih kuat daripada besi.
claims.quote: Among the Troglodytoi (Troglodytes, Cave-Dwellers) this is judged to be the king of beasts, and rightly so, for it possesses the courage of a lion, the speed of a horse, the strength of a bull, and is stronger than iron.

claims.statement: According to the Theoi Project, the bull was probably derived from ancient travellers' accounts of the African buffalo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Theoi Project, banteng ini kemungkinan besar berasal dari catatan para pelancong kuno tentang kerbau Afrika.
claims.quote: The bull was probably derived from ancient travellers' accounts of the African buffalo.

claims.statement: Ga-gorib ('the thrower-down') was a monster in the mythology of the Khoikhoi (called ottentotti in the source).
claims.statement_id: Ga-gorib ("yang menjatuhkan") adalah monster dalam mitologi orang Khoikhoi (dalam sumber disebut ottentotti).
claims.quote: Ga-gorib (letteralmente "colui che butta giù") era un mostro di cui si racconta nella mitologia degli ottentotti.

claims.statement: It lived on the edge of a huge pit and challenged everyone who came to throw stones at it, but the stones bounced back, struck the thrower and knocked him into the pit.
claims.statement_id: Ia tinggal di tepi lubang raksasa dan menantang setiap orang yang lewat untuk melemparinya dengan batu, tetapi batu itu memantul kembali, mengenai pelempar, dan menjatuhkannya ke lubang.
claims.quote: Di lui si racconta che viveva sull'orlo di un pozzo enorme, chiunque giungeva veniva sfidato da lui: dovevano gettragli contro delle pietre, solo che contro il mostro le pietre gettate tornavano indietro e colpiti cadevano nel pozzo.

claims.statement: The hero Heitsi-Eibib came to kill it.
claims.statement_id: Pahlawan Heitsi-Eibib datang untuk membunuhnya.
claims.quote: L'eroe Heitsi-Eibib giunse per ucciderlo

claims.statement: According to the Finnish article, Heitsi-Eibib waited until the monster looked away, then threw a stone that hit it under the ear and pushed it into the pit.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Finlandia, Heitsi-Eibib menunggu sampai monster itu memalingkan pandangan, lalu melempar batu yang mengenai bawah telinganya dan mendorongnya ke dalam lubang.
claims.quote: Ga-goribin kukisti lopulta sankari Heitsi-Ebib, joka malttoi odottaa ja heittää kiven vasta sitten, kun hirviö oli kääntänyt katseensa pois. Hän osui Ga-goribia korvan alle ja työnsi hänet alas kuoppaan.

claims.statement: In the version recorded by Theophilus Hahn, all the people who passed ǂGama-ǂgorib's place were thrown by him into the hole and so perished.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi yang dicatat Theophilus Hahn, semua orang yang melewati tempat ǂGama-ǂgorib dilemparkannya ke dalam lubang dan binasa.
claims.quote: all the people who passed this place were thrown by ... into this hole, and so they perished.

claims.statement: According to Hahn, Heitsi-eibib was first thrown into the hole, but spoke to it, 'Hole of my ancestors, heave up your bottom a little, and give me a lift, that I can jump out'; the hole obeyed and he jumped out.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Hahn, Heitsi-eibib pertama-tama dilemparkan ke dalam lubang, tetapi berkata kepada lubang itu, "Lubang leluhurku, angkatlah dasarmu sedikit dan beri aku dorongan agar aku dapat melompat keluar"; lubang itu menurut dan ia melompat keluar.
claims.quote: And first Heitsi-eibib was thrown into the hole. But he spoke to the hole, and said : " Hole of my ancestors, heave up your bottom a little, and give me a lift, that I can jump out." The hole obeyed, and Heitsi-eibib jumped out

claims.statement: In the third match, according to Hahn, Heitsi-eibib pitched his opponent into the hole by giving him a dead blow behind the ear.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pertandingan ketiga, menurut Hahn, Heitsi-eibib melemparkan lawannya ke dalam lubang dengan pukulan mematikan di belakang telinga.
claims.quote: And they played a third match, and Heitsi-eibib pitched ... into the hole, by giving him a dead blow behind the ear

claims.statement: The ganipote (sometimes spelled galipote or galipotte) is a legendary evil creature from the folklore of the central-western and south-western provinces of France.
claims.statement_id: Ganipote (kadang ditulis galipote atau galipotte) adalah makhluk legendaris jahat dari cerita rakyat provinsi-provinsi Prancis barat-tengah dan barat daya.
claims.quote: La ganipote (parfois orthographiée galipote ou galipotte) est une créature légendaire et maléfique issue du folklore et des légendes des provinces du centre-ouest et du sud-ouest de la France.

claims.statement: This evil, shape-shifting creature tied to witchcraft haunts dark woods, roams the countryside on moonless nights, or prowls around houses before dawn and after sunset.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk jahat yang dapat berubah wujud dan terkait dunia sihir ini menghantui hutan gelap, berkeliaran di pedesaan pada malam tanpa bulan, atau mengintai rumah sebelum fajar dan setelah matahari terbenam.
claims.quote: Créature malfaisante et protéiforme liée au monde de la sorcellerie, elle hanterait les bois sombres, parcourrait la campagne les nuits sans lune ou rôderait autour des demeures habitées le matin avant le jour, et le soir après le coucher du soleil.

claims.statement: It loves terrorising passers-by by leaping violently onto their backs, claws out, clinging and bearing down with all its weight until they suffocate.
claims.statement_id: Ia suka meneror pejalan dengan melompat keras ke punggung mereka dengan cakar terbuka, mencengkeram dan menekan dengan seluruh bobotnya sampai mereka mati tercekik.
claims.quote: s'amuse à terroriser les passants en leur sautant violemment sur le dos, toutes griffes dehors. Elle s'y agrippe et pèse de tout son poids jusqu'à ce qu'ils périssent étouffés.

claims.statement: Besides a wolf, it can take the form of sheep, dogs, goats, hares, pigs, donkeys, cats, horses, oxen, big bats or large birds like geese or swans.
claims.statement_id: Selain serigala, ia dapat berwujud domba, anjing, kambing, kelinci, babi, keledai, kucing, kuda, lembu, kelelawar besar, atau burung besar seperti angsa.
claims.quote: Mais elle peut prendre la forme d'animaux très variés : moutons, chiens, chèvres, lièvres, porcs, ânes, chats, chevaux, bœufs, mais aussi de grandes chauves-souris ou de grands oiseaux semblables à des oies ou des cygnes.

claims.statement: In almost every tale the ganipote is a human temporarily turned into an animal, or somehow embodied in one at night.
claims.statement_id: Dalam hampir semua kisah, ganipote adalah manusia yang untuk sementara berubah menjadi hewan atau menjelma ke tubuh hewan pada malam hari.
claims.quote: Dans presque tous les récits, la ganipote est un être humain transformé temporairement en animal ou s'étant d'une certaine façon incarné en animal pendant la nuit.

claims.statement: The figure is well known in Poitou-Charentes, Touraine, Occitania, and further afield in Forez, the Morvan, even Quebec and the Dominican Republic (the galipote or lugarú).
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini dikenal di Poitou-Charentes, Touraine, Occitania, dan tempat yang lebih jauh seperti Forez, Morvan, bahkan Quebec dan Republik Dominika (galipote atau lugarú).
claims.quote: Es tracta d'un personatge ben conegut a la regió francesa del Poitou-Charentes (Aunis, Saintonge, Angoumois, Poitou), a les veïnes Turena i País Gavai, a Occitània (la Guiena gascona i Alvèrnia) i en llocs més allunyats: Forez (on se l'anomena galipoto), Morvan i fins i tot el Quebec i la República Dominicana (el galipote o lugarú).

claims.statement: There are very similar figures in the legends of Poitou (the garache), Périgord (the leberon) and the Landes (the tac).
claims.statement_id: Ada tokoh dengan ciri sangat mirip dalam legenda Poitou (garache), Périgord (leberon), dan Landes (tac).
claims.quote: Hi ha personatges amb característiques molt similars a les llegendes del Poitou (el garache), el Perigord (el leberon) i les Landes de Gascunya (el tac).

claims.statement: In the Alpine folk traditions of Lombardy, specifically the Val Masino, the Gigiàt is a huge monster whose basically vegetarian diet is supplemented now and then with lone hikers or climbers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi rakyat Alpen Lombardia, khususnya Val Masino, Gigiàt adalah monster raksasa yang pada dasarnya pemakan tumbuhan tetapi sesekali memakan pendaki yang berjalan sendirian.
claims.quote: Il Gigiàt o Gigiàtt sarebbe, nelle tradizioni folkloristiche alpine lombarde, nello specifico della Val Masino, un mostro di proporzioni enormi, che ha la consuetudine di integrare la sua dieta, fondamentalmente vegetariana, con qualche pasto a base di escursionisti o alpinisti solitari

claims.statement: It is probably a cross between an ibex, a deer and a chamois, with very long hair, astonishing speed and such vast size that it can cross a whole valley in a few bounds.
claims.statement_id: Ia mungkin persilangan ibex, rusa, dan chamois berbulu sangat panjang, sangat cepat, dan begitu besar sehingga dapat menyeberangi lembah dengan beberapa lompatan.
claims.quote: Probabilmente è un incrocio fra uno stambecco, un cervo ed un camoscio dal pelo lunghissimo, una velocità impressionante e dalle dimensioni pantagruelliche, tanto da poter attraversare un'intera valle con pochi balzi.

claims.statement: Its figure closely recalls another legendary European mountain animal, the Dahu.
claims.statement_id: Sosoknya sangat mirip hewan gunung legendaris Eropa lain, Dahu.
claims.quote: La sua figura ricorda molto quella di un altro animale montano leggendario europeo: il Dahu.

claims.statement: In the Valtellina dialect gigiàtt means 'strange or undefined thing', reflecting the uncertainty of its features.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dialek Valtellina, gigiàtt berarti "benda aneh atau tak jelas", mencerminkan ketidakpastian ciri-cirinya.
claims.quote: Già dal nome si comprende l'incertezza delle sue caratteristiche, difatti in dialetto valtellinese gigiàtt significa 'cosa strana/indefinita'.

claims.statement: It acts as guardian of those lands and so as judge of the deeds of those who live in or pass through them.
claims.statement_id: Ia berperan sebagai penjaga daerah itu dan hakim atas perbuatan orang yang tinggal atau melintas di sana.
claims.quote: Esso possiede la funzione di guardiano di quelle lande e di conseguenza giudice delle azioni di chi le abita o ci transita.

claims.statement: According to the Lombard article, it is shaped like a big billy goat, perhaps crossed with a chamois, and is known for its speed and size.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Lombard, ia berwujud kambing jantan besar, mungkin persilangan dengan chamois, dan dikenal cepat serta besar.
claims.quote: El gh'ha la forma d'on gross cavron, forsi incrosaa cont on camozz, e l'è cognossuu per el sò vess bell svelt e grand.

claims.statement: A hada (or hade, 'fairy', from Latin fatum, 'fate') is a legendary female being of the Gascon Pyrenees, sometimes called démaïselas (damsels) or damas (ladies).
claims.statement_id: Hada (atau hade, "peri", dari bahasa Latin fatum, "takdir") adalah makhluk perempuan legendaris dari Pyrenees Gascogne, kadang disebut démaïselas (nona) atau damas (nyonya).
claims.quote: Une hada (ou hade, c'est-à-dire une fée, du latin fatum : destin) est un être féminin légendaire des Pyrénées gasconnes que l’on appelle parfois aussi  « démaïselas » (demoiselles) ou « damas » (dames).

claims.statement: Mainly nocturnal, hadas live underground, in caves or near springs and streams.
claims.statement_id: Hada terutama makhluk malam yang tinggal di bawah tanah, di gua, atau dekat mata air dan sungai kecil.
claims.quote: Créatures essentiellement nocturnes, les hadas vivent sous terre, dans des grottes ou auprès des sources et des ruisseaux.

claims.statement: Many places in the Pyrenees and Gascony are linked to them, especially cave and spring names like Hont de las hadas (fairies' spring) and la tutera deras hadas (fairies' cave).
claims.statement_id: Banyak tempat di Pyrenees dan Gascogne dikaitkan dengan mereka, terutama nama gua dan mata air seperti Hont de las hadas (mata air peri) dan la tutera deras hadas (gua peri).
claims.quote: De nombreux lieux dans toutes les Pyrénées et la Gascogne sont associés à leur présence supposée, tout particulièrement le nom de grottes ou de sources, comme le terme « Hont de las hadas » (Fontaine des fées), « la tutera deras hadas » (la grotte des fées)

claims.statement: Hadas are akin to the laminak of Basque mythology, also associated with caves and underground spirits.
claims.statement_id: Hada mirip laminak dalam mitologi Basque, yang juga dikaitkan dengan gua dan roh bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Les hades s'apparentent aux laminak, très présentes dans la mythologie basque, également associées aux grottes et aux esprits souterrains.

claims.statement: Pyrenean imagery sometimes describes a 'hadetta' as a woman with webbed feet.
claims.statement_id: Mitologi Pyrenees kadang menggambarkan "hadetta" sebagai perempuan berkaki selaput.
claims.quote: L’imagerie populaire et la mythologie pyrénéenne décrivent aussi parfois une « hadetta » comme une femme aux pieds palmés.

claims.statement: According to the Catalan article, the Gascon hada is much closer to the Basque lamina, called mora in Upper Aragon, or the Catalan dona d'aigua.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Katalan, hada Gascogne lebih dekat dengan lamina Basque, mora di Aragon Atas, atau dona d'aigua Katalan.
claims.quote: L'hada gascona, en canvi, té molt més a veure amb la lamina basca, anomenada mora a l'Alt Aragó, o la dona d'aigua catalana.

claims.statement: The ipnale (Latin ypnalis or ipnalis, from Greek hypnos, 'sleep') is a legendary serpent of medieval bestiaries.
claims.statement_id: Ipnale (bahasa Latin ypnalis atau ipnalis, dari bahasa Yunani hypnos, "tidur") adalah ular legendaris dalam bestiari abad pertengahan.
claims.quote: L'ipnale (in latino ypnalis o ipnalis; dal greco ὕπνος, hypnos, "sonno") è un serpente leggendario descritto nei bestiari medievali.

claims.statement: Its venom kills by plunging victims into a sleep from which they never wake, hence its name.
claims.statement_id: Bisa ipnale membunuh dengan menenggelamkan korbannya ke dalam tidur tanpa bangun lagi, asal namanya.
claims.quote: In particolare, il veleno dell'ipnale causa la morte facendo sprofondare le sue vittime in un sonno senza risveglio (da cui il nome).

claims.statement: In other versions sleep is not the venom's effect but the moment it chooses to strike, since it moves silently.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi lain, tidur bukan efek bisanya, melainkan saat yang dipilihnya untuk menyerang, karena ia bergerak tanpa suara.
claims.quote: Secondo altre versioni, il sonno non sarebbe l'effetto del veleno del serpente, bensì il momento che questo sceglie per attaccare le sue vittime: l'ipnale si muove infatti silenziosamente.

claims.statement: Tradition holds that Cleopatra's famous asp, by which she had herself bitten to die, was a hypnalis.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, ular aspis terkenal yang dipakai Cleopatra untuk bunuh diri adalah ipnale.
claims.quote: Secondo la tradizione il famoso aspide di Cleopatra, dal quale ella si fece mordere per suicidarsi, era proprio un ipnale.

claims.statement: Boccaccio too names the ipnale explicitly in his commentary on the Divine Comedy when discussing this episode.
claims.statement_id: Boccaccio juga menyebut ipnale secara eksplisit dalam komentarnya tentang Divina Commedia saat membahas peristiwa itu.
claims.quote: Anche Boccaccio, nel suo commento alla Divina commedia, richiama esplicitamente l'ipnale nel riferirsi a questo episodio.

claims.statement: The Medieval Bestiary lists the hypnalis or ypnalis as a variety of asp that kills by sending its victim to sleep; it was this snake that Cleopatra applied to herself.
claims.statement_id: The Medieval Bestiary mendaftar hypnalis atau ypnalis sebagai salah satu jenis asp yang membunuh dengan menidurkan korbannya; inilah ular yang dipakai Cleopatra pada dirinya sendiri.
claims.quote: Hypnalis or ypnalis: kills by sending its victim to sleep. It was this snake that Cleopatra applied to herself

claims.statement: Isidore of Seville (Etymologies 12.4:14) writes that the hypnalis, a type of asp, is so called because it kills by means of sleep; Cleopatra held this snake to herself and was overcome by death as if by sleep.
claims.statement_id: Isidorus dari Sevilla (Etymologies 12.4:14) menulis bahwa hypnalis, sejenis asp, dinamai demikian karena membunuh melalui tidur; Cleopatra memegang ular ini pada dirinya dan mati seolah-olah dalam tidur.
claims.quote: Isidore of Seville [7th century CE] (Etymologies, Book 12, 4:12-16) ... [Book 12, 4:14] The hypnalis, a type of asp, is so called because it kills by means of sleep. Cleopatra held this snake to herself and thus was overcome by death as if by sleep.

claims.statement: Solinus (De mirabilibus mundi 27.31) writes that the hypnale kills with sleep, and that this last, as Cleopatra may bear witness, was purchased for death.
claims.statement_id: Solinus (De mirabilibus mundi 27.31) menulis bahwa hypnale membunuh dengan tidur, dan bahwa ular ini, sebagaimana dapat disaksikan Cleopatra, dibeli untuk kematian.
claims.quote: Gaius Julius Solinus [3rd century CE] (De mirabilibus mundi / Polyhistor, Chapter 27.31-32, 34) ... the hypnale kills with sleep. This last is even -- as Cleopatra may bear witness -- purchased for death.

claims.statement: El Familiar, also known as El cuñado, El Tío or Perro Familiar, is a man-eating familiar spirit whose legend is widespread in the sugar mills of north-western Argentina.
claims.statement_id: El Familiar, dikenal juga sebagai El cuñado, El Tío, atau Perro Familiar, adalah sejenis roh pendamping pemakan manusia yang legendanya tersebar luas di pabrik gula Argentina barat laut.
claims.quote: El Familiar, también conocido como El cuñado, El Tío o Perro Familiar​ es un tipo de espíritu familiar devorador de hombres, cuya leyenda se halla muy difundida en los ingenios azucareros del noroeste argentino.

claims.statement: The best-known version makes it a demonic dog-like creature that gives its owner power and money in exchange, usually, for human lives.
claims.statement_id: Versi paling terkenal menggambarkannya sebagai makhluk iblis berwujud anjing yang memberi kekuasaan dan uang kepada pemiliknya dengan imbalan, biasanya, nyawa manusia.
claims.quote: Se han descrito diferentes versiones de esta entidad, pero la más conocida lo identifica con una especie de criatura demoníaca con aspecto de cánido que da poder y dinero a su poseedor a cambio, generalmente, de vidas humanas.

claims.statement: Sometimes the legend involves a pact between the mill owners and the Devil, securing their status in exchange for their souls and the lives of some workers, taken periodically by the Familiar.
claims.statement_id: Kadang legenda ini melibatkan perjanjian antara pemilik pabrik gula dan Iblis yang menjamin kedudukan mereka dengan imbalan jiwa mereka dan nyawa sebagian pekerja, yang diambil El Familiar secara berkala.
claims.quote: A veces, la leyenda involucra un pacto entre los dueños de los ingenios y el Diablo, que asegura la prevalencia de su estatus socioeconómico a cambio de sus almas y de la vida de algunos de sus trabajadores, arrebatadas periódicamente por el Familiar.

claims.statement: Many disappearances of cane workers at the Ingenio Ledesma and other mills during the Proceso de Reorganización Nacional dictatorship have been linked to the Familiar.
claims.statement_id: Banyak hilangnya pekerja tebu di Ingenio Ledesma dan pabrik lain pada masa kediktatoran Proceso de Reorganización Nacional dikaitkan dengan El Familiar.
claims.quote: Muchas desapariciones de zafreros del Ingenio Ledesma y otros sucedidas durante el Proceso de Reorganización Nacional han sido vinculadas con el accionar del Familiar.

claims.statement: Its most common form is a huge black dog as tall as a man, with blazing eyes that in some accounts shoot fire.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya yang paling umum adalah anjing hitam raksasa setinggi manusia, bermata menyala yang menurut sebagian kisah menyemburkan api.
claims.quote: La forma física més difosa d'aquest ésser monstruós és com un gos negre i enorme, que fins i tot pot arribar a l'altura d'un home. Té una mirada refulgent, fins a arribar a llançar foc pels seus ulls, segons alguns relats.

claims.statement: At night it can take the form of a snake, coiling around the sheds where the workers sleep.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari ia dapat berwujud ular dan melingkari barak tempat para pekerja tidur.
claims.quote: De nit, pot adoptar la forma d'una serp, voltant d'aquesta manera els coberts on dormen els treballadors.

claims.statement: The Ingenio Santa Ana in Tucumán, owned by Clodomiro Hileret, is said to have been the first to obtain its own Familiar.
claims.statement_id: Ingenio Santa Ana di Tucumán milik Clodomiro Hileret disebut sebagai yang pertama memiliki El Familiar sendiri.
claims.quote: S'atribueix a l'Ingenio Santa Ana de Tucumán, propietat de Clodomiro Hileret, d'haver estat el primer a aconseguir el seu propi Familiar

claims.statement: The Karnabo is a creature of Ardennes folklore, said to be the offspring of a supernatural being (a demon or ghoul) and a Bohemian traveller (sometimes called a sorcerer).
claims.statement_id: Karnabo adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Ardennes, konon keturunan makhluk gaib (iblis atau ghoul) dan seorang pengembara Bohemia (kadang disebut penyihir).
claims.quote: The Karnabo is a creature of Ardennes folklore.  It is reputedly the offspring of a supernatural entity (either a demon or a ghoul) and a Bohemian traveller (sometimes said to be a sorcerer).

claims.statement: The Karnabo looks like a man but with an elephant's trunk for a nose and a basilisk's eyes; its breath can paralyse people and kill animals.
claims.statement_id: Karnabo mirip manusia tetapi berhidung belalai gajah dan bermata basilisk; napasnya konon dapat melumpuhkan manusia dan membunuh hewan.
claims.quote: The Karnabo resembles a man but with an elephant's trunk for a nose and the eyes of a basilisk.  The breath of the creature is said to be able to paralyse men and kill animals.

claims.statement: It is said to have abducted a young girl, and her moans and the creature's trumpeting can be heard during thunderstorms.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon menculik seorang gadis, dan saat badai petir rintihan gadis itu dan lengkingan makhluk itu masih terdengar.
claims.quote: It is said to have abducted a young girl and folklore states that her moans and trumpet of the creature can be heard during thunderstorms.

claims.statement: Before leaving for good, the Bohemian passed some powers to the Karnabo, including spell-making and curing whitlow on Good Friday.
claims.statement_id: Sebelum pergi, sang Bohemia mewariskan sebagian kekuatannya kepada Karnabo, termasuk membuat mantra dan menyembuhkan kurap kuku pada Jumat Agung.
claims.quote: Before leaving the area for good he passed some of his powers onto the Karnabo, including the making of spells and the ability to cure whitlow on Good Friday.

claims.statement: By one account it lived for a long time in an abandoned slate quarry near Regniowez.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu kisah ia lama tinggal di tambang batu sabak terbengkalai dekat Regniowez.
claims.quote: By one account it resided for a long time in an abandoned slate quarry near Regniowez.

claims.statement: According to the French article, its head is almost human, but it has a trunk that gives out a shrill whistle, yellow basilisk eyes and dark, rough skin like the walls of its slate quarry.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, kepalanya hampir manusia, tetapi berbelalai yang mengeluarkan siulan melengking, bermata kuning basilisk, dan berkulit gelap kasar seperti dinding tambang sabak tempatnya tinggal.
claims.quote: Il a une tête presque humaine, mais possède une trompe de laquelle sort son sifflement strident, des yeux jaune de basilic et une peau sombre et rugueuse comme les parois de l'ardoisière ou il vit.

claims.statement: The Kuusu was a kind of scarecrow formerly used in the Basque Country to fight evil spirits.
claims.statement_id: Kuusu adalah semacam orang-orangan sawah yang dahulu dipakai di Negeri Basque untuk melawan roh jahat.
claims.quote: El Kuusu era una mena d'espantaocells que es feia servir antigament al País Basc per a combatre els mals esperits.

claims.statement: Basque mythology also has a spirit called Khuso which, according to Julio Caro Baroja, equals the iratxo, also called idittu or etxejaun, a kind of mischievous night sprite.
claims.statement_id: Mitologi Basque juga mengenal roh bernama Khuso yang menurut Julio Caro Baroja setara dengan iratxo, juga disebut idittu atau etxejaun, semacam peri malam yang jahil.
claims.quote: D'altra banda, en la mitologia basca hi ha un geni anomenat Khuso que, segons Julio Caro Baroja, és equiparable a l'iratxo, altrament dit idittu o etxejaun, una mena de follet entremaliat nocturn.

claims.statement: Manuel Agud and Antonio Tovar's Basque Etymological Dictionary defines Khuso as 'scarecrow, ghost', a loan from Béarnese gusot.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Etimologi Basque karya Manuel Agud dan Antonio Tovar mengartikan Khuso sebagai "orang-orangan sawah, hantu", pinjaman dari bahasa Béarn gusot.
claims.quote: Al Diccionario Etimológico Vasco de Manuel Agud i Antonio Tovar, el mot Khuso hi apareix definit com a «espantaocells, fantasma [..] manlleu del bearnès gusot».

claims.statement: According to Labayru Fundazioa, common names for 'bird scarers' in Basque include txorimaloak, txori-jagoleak and kusoak.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Labayru Fundazioa, nama umum untuk "penakut burung" dalam bahasa Basque antara lain txorimaloak, txori-jagoleak, atau kusoak.
claims.quote: Common names for ‘bird scarers’ are espantapájaros, in Spanish, and txorimaloak, txori-jagoleak or kusoak, among others, in Basque.

claims.statement: According to Labayru Fundazioa, homemade humanoid scarecrows placed in open cultivated fields, vineyards and fruit groves have been a common way to protect seed, growing crops and fruit harvests from birds.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Labayru Fundazioa, orang-orangan sawah buatan sendiri berbentuk manusia, ditempatkan di ladang, kebun anggur, dan kebun buah, lazim dipakai untuk melindungi benih, tanaman, dan panen buah dari burung.
claims.quote: Placed in open cultivated fields, vineyards and fruit groves, homemade humanoid scarecrows have been a common way to protect freshly broadcast seed, growing crops and fruit harvests from birds

claims.statement: According to Labayru Fundazioa, scarecrows are traditionally built out of old clothes stuffed with grass or straw and attached to a vertical post driven into the ground.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Labayru Fundazioa, orang-orangan sawah secara tradisional dibuat dari pakaian lama yang diisi rumput atau jerami dan dipasang pada tiang tegak yang ditancapkan ke tanah.
claims.quote: Scarecrows are traditionally built out of old clothes stuffed with grass or straw and attached to a vertical post driven into the ground.

claims.statement: The leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes; from Ancient Greek λεοντοφόνος, 'lion-killer') was a small, most probably legendary animal deadly to lions.
claims.statement_id: Leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes; dari bahasa Yunani Kuno λεοντοφόνος, "pembunuh singa") adalah hewan kecil, kemungkinan besar legendaris, yang mematikan bagi singa.
claims.quote: Leontophone (Leontophonus, Leontophonos, Leophontes, from Ancient Greek: λεοντοφόνος, meaning "lion-killer") was a small animal, most probably legendary, that was deadly to lions.

claims.statement: Its first written record comes from Greco-Roman writers, and it was later known in Medieval bestiaries.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertulis pertamanya berasal dari penulis Yunani-Romawi, dan kemudian ia juga dikenal dalam bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: The first written record is from Greco-Roman writers, but it was also known later during the Medieval period, in Medieval bestiaries.

claims.statement: Leontophones are described as fatally poisonous to lions: a lion dies merely by biting one.
claims.statement_id: Leontophone digambarkan sangat beracun bagi singa: singa akan mati hanya dengan menggigitnya.
claims.quote: Leontophones are described as fatally poisonous to lions, such that a lion will die if it merely bites a leontophone.

claims.statement: In the proper ritual its flesh is burned and the ashes sprinkled on meat left at a crossroads; a lion eating even a little of it dies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ritual yang tepat, daging leontophone dibakar dan abunya ditaburkan pada sepotong daging yang diletakkan di persimpangan jalan; singa yang memakannya sedikit saja akan mati.
claims.quote: In a proper ritual, the leontophone's flesh is burned and its ashes are sprinkled on a piece of meat, which is placed at a crossroad; if a lion eats even a small amount of the tainted meat, it dies.

claims.statement: Some sources say the lion flees instead and attacks only when cornered, since the leontophone's urine is also deadly to lions.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sumber menyebut singa justru lari darinya dan hanya menyerang bila terdesak, karena air seni leontophone juga mematikan bagi singa.
claims.quote: However, some sources state that the lion will instead flee from the small creature, only attacking and killing it when left with no option to flee (since attacking the leontophone may cause it to urinate, and the urine of the leontophone is also fatally poisonous to lions).

claims.statement: Lions hate leontophones; confronted with one, they often hunt and kill it, tearing it with their claws rather than biting.
claims.statement_id: Singa membenci leontophone; bila berhadapan, singa sering memburu dan membunuhnya dengan mencabik memakai cakar, bukan menggigit.
claims.quote: Likewise, due to the danger they pose to lions, lions instinctively hate leontophones. Confronted by a leontophone, they often hunt and kill them, tearing them apart with their claws rather than biting them.

claims.statement: No source gives a definite description of its appearance; some guess a small boar or small bear, others that it is serpentine.
claims.statement_id: Tidak ada sumber yang memberi gambaran pasti tentang wujudnya; sebagian menduga mirip babi hutan kecil atau beruang kecil, yang lain menduga mirip ular.
claims.quote: Though no sources give a definite depiction of the leontophone's appearance, some sources speculate that the creature looks like a small boar or a small bear, while others speculate that it is serpentine

claims.statement: The Dutch article also says lions hate leontophones and hunt them, tearing them with their claws rather than biting.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Belanda juga menyebut singa membenci leontophone dan memburunya, mencabiknya dengan cakar alih-alih menggigit.
claims.quote: Leeuwen haten leontophonen. Ze jagen erop en doden hen, eerder door ze te verscheuren met hun klauwen, dan ze te bijten.

claims.statement: The Longana (in places such as Oltrepiave and Auronzo called Anguana) is a female water creature of the tradition of Cadore and Comelico, especially Lozzo di Cadore.
claims.statement_id: Longana (di beberapa tempat seperti Oltrepiave dan Auronzo disebut Anguana) adalah makhluk air perempuan dari tradisi Cadore dan Comelico, terutama Lozzo di Cadore.
claims.quote: Il nome Longana (o a seconda del luogo, come in Oltrepiave e Auronzo  Anguana) indica una creatura acquatica fantastica di sesso femminile tipica della tradizione del Cadore e Comelico (soprattutto Lozzo di Cadore).

claims.statement: They live in groups in caves or rock clefts named after them, like the Bùs de le Longane cleft at Vallesella and the Sass de le Longane rock at Lozzo.
claims.statement_id: Mereka hidup berkelompok di gua atau celah batu yang dinamai menurut mereka, seperti celah Bùs de le Longane di Vallesella dan batu Sass de le Longane di Lozzo.
claims.quote: Nella tradizione questo essere suole vivere in gruppo in grotte o anfratti rocciosi che nella toponimia locale prendono il suo nome: esiste a Vallesella un anfratto detto "Bùs de le Longane" e a Lozzo un sasso detto "Sass de le Longane".

claims.statement: They are depicted as very beautiful, intelligent women with goat legs whose dual nature links them directly to the forest spirit, giving them extraordinary power to foretell natural events.
claims.statement_id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai perempuan sangat cantik dan cerdas berkaki kambing, yang karena sifat gandanya berhubungan langsung dengan roh hutan yang memberi mereka kemampuan luar biasa meramalkan peristiwa alam.
claims.quote: Sono raffigurate come donne bellissime e molto intelligenti, ma con arti inferiori di capra, e poste dalla loro duplice natura in diretta comunicazione con lo spirito silvestre che conferisce loro poteri straordinari di predizione degli eventi naturali.

claims.statement: In the Domegge version a man, ancestor of the Da Deppo family, falls for a Longana and marries her on condition he never reminds her of her origins.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Domegge, seorang lelaki, leluhur keluarga Da Deppo, jatuh cinta pada seorang Longana dan menikahinya dengan syarat ia tidak pernah mengungkit asal-usul istrinya.
claims.quote: Nella versione domeggese della leggenda un uomo, capostipite della importante famiglia Da Deppo, si invaghisce di una Longana e la fa sua sposa, a patto che lui non le ricordi mai le sue origini.

claims.statement: After prosperous years the Longana reaps the wheat early because she foresaw a storm; her husband insults her as 'goat-foot' and she vanishes into the woods, leaving their children.
claims.statement_id: Setelah bertahun-tahun makmur, Longana memanen gandum lebih awal karena meramalkan badai; suaminya menghinanya dengan sebutan "kaki kambing", lalu ia menghilang ke hutan meninggalkan anak-anak mereka.
claims.quote: Dopo anni prosperi, in seguito a una mietitura precoce del grano da parte della Longana che aveva previsto una tempesta, l'uomo la insulta chiamandola "piè di capra" e la Longana sparisce nei boschi lasciando i figli nati dall'unione.

claims.statement: In nearby Comelico some suggest they were really the women of a Hungarian group that migrated there and lived by timber and herding at the forest's edge.
claims.statement_id: Di Comelico, sebagian orang menduga mereka sebenarnya perempuan dari suatu kelompok Hungaria yang bermigrasi ke sana dan hidup dari kayu serta penggembalaan di tepi hutan.
claims.quote: Nel vicino Comelico alcuni suggeriscono che le stesse fossero in realtà le rappresentanti femminili di una popolazione ungara migrata in quei territori che viveva di legname e pastorizia al margine del bosco

claims.statement: The Longana legend contains many oral-tradition topoi: the woman's ambiguity, the half-human half-animal woodland nature, and the purification rituals of night bathing these creatures practised.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Longana memuat banyak topos tradisi lisan: ambiguitas perempuan, sifat hutan setengah manusia setengah hewan, dan ritual penyucian berupa mandi malam yang biasa mereka lakukan.
claims.quote: Nella leggenda delle Longane appaiono molti "topos" delle tradizioni orali: l'ambiguità della donna, la natura silvana mezzo umano/mezzo animale, i rituali di purificazione nei bagni notturni che solevano praticare queste creature.

claims.statement: The Macedonian article also calls the Longana a legendary female water being in the legends of the people of Cadore, Italy.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Makedonia juga menyebut Longana makhluk air legendaris perempuan dalam legenda orang Cadore, Italia.
claims.quote: Лонгана е легендарно водно суштество од женски род. Лонганите се споменуваат во легендите за луѓето од Кадоре, Италија.

issues.message: Mengusulkan tradisi baru: "Cerita rakyat Wallonia dan Flandria".

claims.statement: The macrâle (also makrâlle, macralle, macrale, or makralle in Flemish) is the name for a witch in Wallonia, Flanders and the Ardennes.
claims.statement_id: Macrâle (juga makrâlle, macralle, macrale, atau makralle dalam bahasa Flam) adalah sebutan untuk penyihir perempuan di Wallonia, Flandria, dan Ardennes.
claims.quote: La macrâle, makrâlle, macralle, macrale (ou makralle en flamand) désigne une sorcière en Wallonie, en Flandre et dans les Ardennes.

claims.statement: The term macrâle comes from the Walloon of Liège and Luxembourg; its masculine form, macrê, means a male sorcerer.
claims.statement_id: Istilah macrâle berasal dari bahasa Walloon Liège dan Luxembourg; bentuk maskulinnya, macrê, berarti penyihir laki-laki.
claims.quote: Le terme macrâle provient du wallon liégeois et luxembourgeois et a comme masculin le terme macrê qui quant à lui signifie sorcier.

claims.statement: According to Pierre Dubois, the macrâle is a mix of elf and witch who loves sabbaths and roams at night casting a host of curses.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Pierre Dubois, macrâle adalah campuran elf dan penyihir yang menyukai sabat dan berkeliaran pada malam hari sambil melontarkan berbagai kutukan.
claims.quote: Selon Pierre Dubois, la macrâle est un mélange d'elfe et de sorcière qui affectionne les sabbats, et se promène durant la nuit en lançant un florilège de maléfices.

claims.statement: The macrâle is blamed for many ills such as the coming of winter, floods and epidemics; they people the forests like other creatures of Belgian and Ardennes folklore (nutons, sottai, Bayard).
claims.statement_id: Macrâle dituduh menyebabkan banyak bencana seperti datangnya musim dingin, banjir, dan wabah; mereka menghuni hutan seperti makhluk lain dalam cerita rakyat Belgia dan Ardennes (nuton, sottai, Bayard).
claims.quote: La macrâle est accusée d'être responsable de bien des maux, tels que la venue de l'hiver, des inondations et des épidémies. Elles peuplent les forêts comme d'autres créatures du folklore belge et ardennais (nutons, sottai, Bayard).

claims.statement: Many folklore groups portray macrâles and witches, notably in the sabbaths of Haccourt, Vielsalm and Ellezelles (where they are called chorchîles).
claims.statement_id: Banyak kelompok folklor memerankan macrâle dan penyihir, antara lain dalam sabat di Haccourt, Vielsalm, dan Ellezelles (tempat mereka disebut chorchîles).
claims.quote: De nombreux groupes folkloriques représentent des macrales et sorcières, notamment dans les sabbats de Haccourt, Vielsalm, Ellezelles (où elles sont appelées "chorchîles")

claims.statement: The folklore group Macralles du val de Salm at Vielsalm was founded in 1955 in honour of a local legend about the real person Marie-Joseph-Augustine Lemoine, called Gustine Maka.
claims.statement_id: Kelompok folklor Macralles du val de Salm di Vielsalm didirikan pada 1955 untuk menghormati legenda setempat tentang tokoh nyata Marie-Joseph-Augustine Lemoine, yang dijuluki Gustine Maka.
claims.quote: Les Macralles du val de Salm (ou de Vielsam) est un groupe folklorique fondé en 1955 et qui a été créé en l'honneur d'une légende locale, autour de la personnalité bien réelle de Marie-Joseph-Augustine Lemoine dite Gustine Maka.

claims.statement: The Dutch article likewise says makrallen (Flemish) or macrâles (Walloon) comes from a Liège Walloon word for witch.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Belanda juga menyebut makrallen (Flam) atau macrâles (Walloon) berasal dari kata Walloon Liège untuk penyihir perempuan.
claims.quote: De makrallen in het Vlaams, les macrâles, macralles ou makrâlles in het Waals, komt van een Luiks-Waals woord voor heks.

claims.statement: Mama 'e su Sole is a creature typical of Sardinian folklore, born to warn children against staying in the sun in the hottest hours of the day.
claims.statement_id: Mama 'e su Sole adalah makhluk khas cerita rakyat Sardinia yang muncul untuk memperingatkan anak-anak akan bahaya berada di bawah matahari pada jam-jam terpanas.
claims.quote: Mama 'e su Sole è una creatura tipica del folklore sardo, nata per mettere in guardia i bambini dal rischio di restare al sole nelle ore più calde della giornata.

claims.statement: Conceptually it resembles the uomo nero or the gatto mammone.
claims.statement_id: Secara konsep ia mirip uomo nero atau gatto mammone.
claims.quote: Concettualmente è simile all'uomo nero o al gatto mammone.

claims.statement: Sa Mama 'e su Sole (the Mother of the Sun) is identified with a very beautiful woman who appears in summer from noon until about 16:00, the hottest hours.
claims.statement_id: Sa Mama 'e su Sole (Ibu Matahari) diidentikkan dengan perempuan sangat cantik yang muncul pada musim panas, dari tengah hari sampai sekitar pukul 16, jam-jam terpanas.
claims.quote: (la Madre del Sole) è identificata con una donna bellissima che appare d'estate, dopo mezzogiorno fino circa alle 16 del pomeriggio (le ore più calde della giornata).

claims.statement: The legend says that if she meets a child playing in the street against its parents' wishes, she chases it down, touches its forehead leaving a mark, and the child is at once seized by a fever (halentura) lasting some days.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, bila ia menemukan anak yang bermain di jalan karena tidak menuruti orang tuanya, ia mengejarnya, menyentuh dahinya hingga meninggalkan tanda, dan anak itu segera terserang demam (halentura) selama beberapa hari.
claims.quote: La leggenda dice che se la Mama 'e su Sole incontra un bambino per strada a giocare, disubbidendo ai genitori, lo rincorreva fino a raggiungerlo, gli tocca la fronte lasciandogli un segno e subito il bambino viene assalito da una febbre (halentura), che dura alcuni giorni.

claims.statement: The figure was also created to explain fever caused by long exposure to the sun during a heatwave.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh ini juga diciptakan untuk menjelaskan demam akibat terlalu lama terpapar matahari pada masa panas terik.
claims.quote: Venne creato questo personaggio, anche per spiegare il fenomeno della febbre, dovuta in seguito a una prolungata esposizione al sole in un periodo di forte canicola.

claims.statement: In some Sardinian villages there is said also to be sa Mama 'e su Frittu (the Mother of the Cold), her sister and winter counterpart.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa desa Sardinia diceritakan pula adanya sa Mama 'e su Frittu (Ibu Dingin), saudarinya dan padanannya pada musim dingin.
claims.quote: si narra che esistesse anche sa Mama 'e su Frittu [pron. sa Mamma 'e su Vrittu] (la Madre del Freddo), sua sorella e controparte invernale.

claims.statement: There were also sa Mama 'e su Fogu (the Mother of Fire), to explain fires to children, and sa Mama 'e su Ventu (the Mother of the Wind), who appeared when the strong Maestrale or Tramontana blew.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula sa Mama 'e su Fogu (Ibu Api) untuk menjelaskan kebakaran kepada anak-anak, dan sa Mama 'e su Ventu (Ibu Angin) yang muncul saat angin Maestrale atau Tramontana bertiup kencang.
claims.quote: Poi c'erano sa Mama 'e su Fogu [pron. sa Mamma 'e su Vógu] (la Madre del Fuoco), per spiegare ai bimbi il fenomeno degli incendi, e sa Mama 'e su Ventu [pron. sa Mamma 'e su Ventu] (la Madre del Vento), la quale appariva quando soffiavano il forte Maestrale o la Tramontana.

claims.statement: The Sardinian-language article says this tale was known in every village throughout Sardinia.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Sardinia menyebut kisah ini dikenal di setiap desa di seluruh Sardinia.
claims.quote: Custa paristoria fit connotta in cada bidda peri tottu sa Sardigna.

claims.statement: Mandrònius (Mandròni in the Aranese version, Mandroni in Catalan) is a giant of the Gascon mythology of the Val d'Aran.
claims.statement_id: Mandrònius (Mandròni dalam versi Aran, Mandroni dalam bahasa Katalan) adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Gascon khas Val d'Aran.
claims.quote: Mandrònius, o Mandròni en versió aranesa –Mandroni en català–, és un gegant de la mitologia gascona pròpia de la Vall d'Aran.

claims.statement: By the legend Mandrònius was a man about three metres tall who lived in a cave near Betlan and led the people of the Val d'Aran against the Romans, winning several battles and respect for his courage.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Mandrònius adalah lelaki setinggi sekitar tiga meter yang tinggal di gua dekat Betlan dan memimpin penduduk Val d'Aran melawan bangsa Romawi, menang dalam beberapa pertempuran dan dihormati karena keberaniannya.
claims.quote: Segons diu la llegenda, Mandrònius era un home d'aproximadament tres metres d'altura. Es diu que vivia en una cova a prop de Betlan i va liderar els habitants de la Vall d'Aran en la lluita contra els romans, obtenint victòries en diverses batalles i guanyant-se el respecte per la seva valentia.

claims.statement: He fell in love with an Aranese woman and they had a daughter; when the Romans abducted the valley's women, he took revenge by wrecking the enemy camp and sending the soldiers' ears to Rome as a warning.
claims.statement_id: Ia jatuh cinta pada perempuan Aran dan mempunyai seorang putri; ketika bangsa Romawi menculik perempuan lembah itu, ia membalas dengan menghancurkan perkemahan musuh dan mengirim telinga para prajurit ke Roma sebagai peringatan.
claims.quote: Mandrònius es va enamorar d'una dona aranesa i van tenir una filla junts. Quan els romans van segrestar les dones de la vall, Mandrònius es va venjar devastant el campament enemic i enviant les orelles dels soldats com a advertència a Roma.

claims.statement: His death is debated: some versions say he died peacefully in his cave with his family, others that the people of Garòs, who saw him as a threat, killed him.
claims.statement_id: Kematiannya diperdebatkan: sebagian versi menyebut ia wafat dengan tenang di guanya bersama keluarganya, versi lain menyebut ia dibunuh penduduk Garòs yang menganggapnya ancaman.
